chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Zareeh, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Saeed Al-Khudry was from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he was straightforward/upright, but he was in agony/died for three days. So his family washed him, then he was carried to his prayer-mat, and he died in it.'
ai.seo_question: What happened to Abu Saeed Al-Khudry when he was dying according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practice of placing the dying near their place of worship, specifically noting that Abu Saeed Al-Khudry, a companion known for his uprightness, passed away on his prayer-mat after three days of intense suffering. The chain of transmission through al-Husayn ibn Uthman and Dharih underscores the reliability of this report within the Shia scholarly tradition, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the final moments in a sacred space.
